title: Biolayer Interferometry for DNA-Protein Interactions
author: John K Barrows
materials: Our laboratory uses DNA probes derived from the ST2R24 selection template (sequence details can be found at: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0159408 ) to identify the preferred binding sequence of thermophilic transcription factors. The design of related fluorophore-labeled modular selection templates and their synthesis has been described ( https://dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wfjfbkn ). These DNAs are approximately 50-70 bp in length and have been used extensively for BLI analysis.

Following manufacturer's guidelines ( https://doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ch7t9m ), assemble a 50 μL PCR reaction containing: 1× NEB Standard Taq Reaction Buffer, 200 μM dNTPs, 100 nM 5′ biotin-labeled primer BIO_ST2R and 100 nM unlabeled primer ST2L, 4 ng ST2-derived template DNA, and 1.25 units Taq DNA polymerase in a 0.2 mL thin-wall PCR tube on ice. Mix thoroughly by pipetting. The biotinylated BIO_ST2R primer was purchased from Integrated DNA Technologies and contains a Biotin_dT at the 5' end. More information about biotin-conjugated nucleotides from Integrated DNA Technologies can be found at: https://www.idtdna.com/pages/education/decoded/article/which-biotin-modification-to-use- . For an example experiment used throughout this protocol, we will perform BLI with the consensus binding sequence our laboratory identified for the Thermus thermophilus transcriptional regulation SbtR (Van Dyke MW et al. Identification of Preferred DNA-Binding Sites for the Thermus thermophilus Transcriptional Regulator SbtR by the Combinatorial Approach REPSA. PLoS One. 2016 Jul 18;11(7):e0159408. DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0159408. PMID: 27428627; PMCID: PMC4948773.). The ST2-derived template DNA used for our PCR contains the published consensus sequence, and the resulting PCR product will be further denoted as biotinylated-WT_SbtR.

The results of the analysis will be presented in a table and include binding kinetics, confidence intervals, and goodness of fit parameters. The results can also be presented in graphical form under the "Graphs" tab. The results of our example experiment are presented in Table 1 and Figure 6 below. Kon (min-1*M-1) Koff (min-1) Kd (nM) R-squared 1 282500 0.000234 0.827 0.96 Table 1: Association and dissociation rates for SbtR binding to its consensus sequence. Figure 6: Graphical representation of BLI results showing binding of the thermophilic protein, SbtR, to its consensus DNA-binding sequence. Closed circles indicate individual data points and solid lines represent the nonlinear regression line of best fit.

steps.title: Program thermal cycler for PCR
steps.instruction: Program the Bio‑Rad C1000 Touch™ thermal cycler with a heated lid set to 105 °C using the following cycling conditions: 95 °C for 2 min; then 19 cycles of 95 °C for 30 s, 54 °C for 30 s, 68 °C for 1 min; followed by 68 °C for 2 min and hold at 4 °C indefinitely.

steps.title: Amplify biotinylated DNA probes
steps.instruction: Run the PCR using the program above to generate biotinylated DNA; optionally analyse the PCR products by native PAGE with ethidium bromide staining to confirm a single double‑stranded band.

steps.title: Prepare BLI‑100 buffer (4 mL)
steps.instruction: Make BLI‑100 buffer (20 mM Tris, pH 7.5; 100 mM NaCl; 1 mM EDTA; 0.05 % Tween‑20). Prepare 4 mL (enough for 32 wells × 200 µL + extra). Add 200 µL of this buffer to each well in columns 2, 3, and 4 of a Greiner Bio 96‑well flat‑bottom plate (rows A‑D).

steps.title: Prepare DNA‑BLI‑100 master mix
steps.instruction: Combine 1 mL BLI‑100 buffer with 125 ng biotinylated‑WT_SbtR DNA (≈6 µL of PCR product, ~25 ng per well) to make a master mix. Aliquot 200 µL of this mix into each well of column 1 (rows A‑D).

steps.title: Create protein dilution series
steps.instruction: Dilute SbtR protein stock to 900 nM in BLI‑100 buffer. Add 100 µL of this protein‑BLI‑100 mixture to well A3 (which already contains 200 µL BLI‑100) and mix. Transfer 100 µL from A3 to B3, mix; transfer 100 µL from B3 to C3, mix; transfer 100 µL from C3 to D3, mix and discard 100 µL from D3 to leave 200 µL total. Final concentrations will be A3 = 300 nM, B3 = 100 nM, C3 = 33.3 nM, D3 = 11.1 nM.

steps.title: Load Octet RED96e with plate and sensors
steps.instruction: Place the prepared 96‑well plate firmly into the ForteBio Octet RED96e. Insert the Streptavidin Dip and Read™ biosensor tray so that sensors align with wells A1‑A4.

steps.title: Start Data Acquisition software
steps.instruction: Close the instrument door, launch Data Acquisition 12.0 on the connected computer; the system will perform a ~30 s self‑initialisation check.

steps.title: Create new blank kinetics experiment
steps.instruction: In the Experiment Wizard, click New Kinetics Experiment → Basic Kinetics → Blank Experiment. This opens the five tabs: Plate Definition, Assay Definition, Sensor Alignment, Review Experiment, Run Experiment.

steps.title: Define plate layout
steps.instruction: In Plate Definition, highlight wells A1‑D4 (columns 1‑4, rows A‑D). Change well types: A1‑A4 → “Load” (DNA); B1‑B4 and D1‑D4 → “Buffer”; C1‑C4 → “Sample” (protein). Enter sample IDs and concentrations as needed.

steps.title: Program assay steps
steps.instruction:
In Assay Definition, add the following steps to the Step Data List (all with shake speed 1000):
1. Sensor Check – 500 s (Column 2, Buffer)
2. Loading – 900 s (Column 1, DNA)
3. Baseline – 300 s (Column 2, Buffer)
4. Association – 500 s (Column 3, Protein)
5. Dissociation – 900 s (Column 5, Buffer).
Create the first step, then use “Replicate → Append to current assay” three times to generate four additional steps, editing each to match the table above.

steps.title: Align biosensors in tray
steps.instruction: In Sensor Alignment, verify that the four biosensor tips are positioned in the tray slots corresponding to wells A1‑A4 before proceeding.

steps.title: Review experimental design
steps.instruction: Use the black arrows in the Review Experiment tab to confirm the sequence: Sensor Check (Column 2), Loading (Column 1), Baseline (Column 2), Association (Column 3), Dissociation (Column 5).

steps.title: Run BLI experiment and save data
steps.instruction: In Run Experiment, press the green GO button. The run will last ~54 min (≈0:53:04). Save the data to a specified folder using the default run settings or adjust as desired.

steps.title: Open Data Analysis and load experiment
steps.instruction: Launch ForteBio Data Analysis 12.0, choose File → Load a Folder, and select the folder saved in the previous step.

steps.title: Export raw data
steps.instruction: In the Processing tab, click “Save Raw Data”. This creates a file named RawData0.xls containing time (seconds) and shift (nm) for each measurement.

steps.title: Prepare association/dissociation table
steps.instruction: In a spreadsheet, extract rows from time ≥ 1700 s (the start of the Association step). Subtract the shift value at 1700 s from all subsequent shift values so the first point is 0 nm. Create a Time column starting at 0 and increasing by 0.2 s (Octet reads every 0.2 s). Label each data column with the corresponding protein concentration (nM).

steps.title: Import data into GraphPad Prism
steps.instruction: Open GraphPad Prism 9.2.0 (332). Create a new XY table, select “Numbers” for X and “Enter and plot a single Y value for each point” for Y. Paste the processed Association and Dissociation data: X = time (s) starting at 0, Y = shift (nm) for each concentration column. Ensure column titles contain the protein concentration in nM.

steps.title: Perform nonlinear regression
steps.instruction:
In Prism, click Analyze → XY analyses → Nonlinear regression (curve fit). Choose Model → Binding – Kinetics → Association then dissociation. In the Constrain tab set:
- HotNM = “Data set constant (from column title)”.
- Kon and Koff = “Shared value for all data sets”.
- Time0 = “Constant equal to” 500 (seconds, the start of dissociation). Click OK to run the fit.
